title: EIP-8374: Persist Warm Access Sets Across Reverts
description: Accessed addresses and storage keys stay warm when a call frame reverts, as the data is already loaded by the client
author: Dragan Rakita (@rakita)
laymanDescription: Reading state for the first time costs more than reading it again, because the client has to fetch it from disk. Today that discount is thrown away when a call reverts, even though the data is still in memory. This proposal keeps it for the rest of the transaction.
benefits: Charges the second read what it actually costs the client, which is nearly nothing
No transaction becomes more expensive; costs either fall or stay the same
Access sets leave the state journal entirely, becoming append-only per transaction
tradeoffs: Contracts that measure exact gas costs of accesses after a revert will see different numbers
A transaction can warm state inside a frame it then reverts and read it cheaply after
